evidence.text: The LORD reigns, let the earth rejoice; let the distant shores be glad.
The mountains melt like wax at the presence of the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.
Zion hears and rejoices, and the towns of Judah exult because of Your judgments, O LORD.
For You, O LORD, are Most High over all the earth; You are exalted far above all gods.
Hate evil, O you who love the LORD! He preserves the souls of His saints; He delivers them from the hand of the wicked.
Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous ones, and praise His holy name.

Darkness and Light
Darkness
Darkness is the absence of light. There was no light until God commanded that light appear. He then made a distinction between light and its absence (
). The ninth plague on Egypt was three days of intense darkness, a complete absence of light (
There is a darkness surrounding God (
); he dwells in thick darkness (
), and thick darkness is under his feet (
). God is unknowable unless he reveals himself.
Darkness often stands for distress and anxiety, or for the confusion and destruction experienced by the wicked (
For Job, darkness was like nothingness (
). It points to death, a land of shadows and gloom, the dwelling place of the dead far from the light of day (
Evil takes place under the cover of darkness (
), but darkness cannot be a hiding place from God (
). Darkness often depicts ignorance of God’s will: Knowledge of God is “light,” so lack of knowledge is “darkness” (
). Moral depravity is described as darkness (
). In the New Testament, darkness is also a metaphor for spiritual ignorance (
). Those who come to know God come out of darkness (
A major theme of the Old Testament prophets was the Day of the Lord, which was often associated with darkness (
). The New Testament also links darkness with judgment (
